title: Listening to the Public
summaries: Collected public feedback through surveys and interactive activities, revealing demand for portable respiratory pathogen testing.

title: Random Interviews at the Third Hospital of Harbin Medical University
summaries: Visited pediatric and geriatric departments, identifying mobility barriers and cross-infection risks that support local screening.

title: Interviews with Nursing Home Care Workers and Residents
summaries: Interviewed nursing home staff and residents, identifying the need for simple, rapid, on-site infection screening.

title: Interview with Professor Li Juan, Former Dean of the School of Public Health, Jilin University
summaries: Discussed primary-care needs with Dean Juan Li, defining a portable, rapid, multiplex pathogen detection goal.

title: Roundtable with Public Health and Disease Control Experts
summaries: Consulted disease-control experts to position ByeGerm as a community early-warning node and draft an emergency response guide.

title: Interview with Vice Dean Changgui Kou of the School of Public Health, Jilin University
summaries: Used epidemiological guidance to select five respiratory targets: RSV, hMPV-B, SPN, BP, and HI.

title: Interview with Dr. Junyao Li, Respiratory Medicine
summaries: Consulted respiratory clinicians to define ByeGerm as an out-of-hospital preliminary screening tool, not a laboratory replacement.

title: Interview with Dr. Huimin Li, Laboratory Medicine
summaries: Confirmed that on-site screening should complement, not replace, standardized laboratory confirmation.

title: Interview with Dr. Shangwei Ji, Infectious Diseases
summaries: Discussed on-site risk stratification to guide observation, isolation, and referral decisions.

title: Interview with Dr. Xin Tian, Pediatrics
summaries: Identified kindergarten and home screening opportunities to help caregivers recognize pediatric respiratory risks earlier.

title: Interview with Professor X. Chris Le, University of Alberta
summaries: Adopted expert advice to pursue a portable, one-pot RPA–CRISPR/Cas12a assay instead of conventional PCR.

title: Interview with Professor Tianyi Zhao, Harbin Institute of Technology
summaries: Discussed DNABERT-based machine learning to improve candidate sequence screening and multiplex detection specificity.

title: Interview with Professor Xingfang Li, University of Alberta
summaries: Discussed molecular docking and dynamics simulations to assess candidate structural stability before wet-lab experiments.

title: Interview with Professor Tsan-Yuk Lam, University of Hong Kong
summaries: Developed optimization strategies for one-pot interference using single-factor gradients and comprehensive controls.

title: Interview with Professor Zheng Hu and Professor Yingtao Zhang, Harbin Institute of Technology
summaries: Integrated expert recommendations on temperature control, microcomputing, and computer vision for automated fluorescence analysis.

title: Collecting First-Generation Instrument Feedback from Nursing Homes
summaries: Nursing-home trials revealed limitations of single-channel testing, motivating a multi-channel instrument upgrade.

title: Collecting First-Generation Instrument Feedback from Kindergartens
summaries: Kindergarten feedback highlighted the need for faster, higher-throughput screening during sudden fevers.

title: Interview with Professor Ying Mou, Zhejiang University
summaries: Implemented rotational switching and thermal isolation recommendations in the second-generation 15-well instrument.

title: The “Auditory and Tactile” Blind-Testing Box for Older Adults and The “Monster Capture” Sticker Wall for Children
summaries: Collected 60 votes from older adults, with 70% positive feedback on device usability.
Used sticker voting with 50 children, finding 64% expressed positive feelings toward screening.

title: The Retrospective Empathy Survey for Patients
summaries: Surveyed 200 patients; 90% preferred mobile displays and 85% reported reduced anxiety with bedside testing.

title: Interview with Director Linshen Xie, West China Fourth Hospital of Sichuan University
summaries: Discussed quality control, exception handling, data traceability, and public health integration for responsible deployment.

title: Communication with Medical Device Manufacturing Enterprise
summaries: Reviewed production feasibility, material safety, certification, and cost reduction with medical device engineers.

title: Age-Adapted and Child-Friendly Science Education
summaries: Delivered age-adapted science education, increasing voluntary testing acceptance to 93% among older adults and 95% among children.

title: Respiratory Virus Detection Strategy Card Game Experience
summaries: Created a respiratory virus card game to explain transmission and detection through playful participation.

title: Volunteer Science Education in Tang County, Hebei
summaries: Introduced device models and public health concepts in remote classrooms through demonstrations and hands-on learning.

title: Interview with Vice President Wei Ye, Nanjing Second Hospital
summaries: Defined single-channel use for homes and small institutions and multi-channel screening for communities and disease-control centers.

title: Wonderful Building Blocks of Life — Kindergarten Synthetic Biology
summaries: Introduced synthetic biology to preschool children through storytelling, child-safe DNA crafts, and RNA role-play.

title: Beyond Mountains and Seas — Science in County Communities
summaries: Brought interactive synthetic biology lessons and hands-on models to students in county-level communities.

title: Wisdom in Silver Years — Science with Older Adults
summaries: Engaged older adults through tactile models, fermentation analogies, and discussions of respiratory health technologies.

title: Sound as a Bridge — Accessible Science for People with Visual Impairments
summaries: Co-designed a multisensory synthetic biology workshop and accessible handbook for participants with visual impairments.

title: A Dialogue Across Continents — Global Youth Exchange
summaries: Connected international students through roundtables and cross-cultural design challenges on synthetic biology applications.

title: Lighting a Spark in the Community — Public Health Dialogue
summaries: Held community health salons with frontline professionals to discuss biosensors, screening needs, and deployment pathways.

title: CCiC & APIc Conferences
summaries: Exchanged technical and regulatory perspectives with iGEM teams at CCiC and APIc conferences.

title: BioAI Agent Exchange and Summer Dry-Lab Camp
summaries: Collaborated on BioAI Agent discussions and a dry-lab outreach lecture to share computational biology skills.

title: Dialogue with ZJUT-China at the Bio-manufacturing Expo
summaries: Exchanged project ideas with ZJUT-China at the Bio-manufacturing Expo, inspiring participatory outreach formats.

title: iGEM New Team Development and Knowledge Transfer Handbook
summaries: Co-developed an iGEM team handbook with JLU-FBH to share management, troubleshooting, and knowledge-transfer practices.

title: AI × Synthetic Biology Collaborative Science Communication Handbook
summaries: Co-authored an AI–synthetic biology handbook with four iGEM teams, covering opportunities, limitations, and ethical considerations.

title: SBti Interactive Public Engagement
summaries: Developed the SBti interactive survey to gather public attitudes and tailor synthetic biology communication.

title: Tower-Defense Synthetic Biology Education Game
summaries: Created an open-source tower-defense game to make synthetic biology mechanisms accessible through play.

title: Hike with Love · Embrace the Future — Social Inclusion
summaries: Supported 100 young people with special needs through medical assistance and science outreach during an inclusive hike.
